findings.consequence: Pallet jams at the conveyor entry are never detected. The conveyor motor continues running against jammed pallets, risking mechanical damage, motor overload, and pallet pileups without raising an alarm.
findings.evidence: Lint L005 reports conveyor entry photo-eye PE-1002 (X11) is unused. Cause-effect CE-ST10-03 and narrative §3 require stopping conveyor motor M-1001 (Y10) and raising a latched jam alarm when PE-1002 is blocked for >5.0 s (parameter jam_time = 5.0 s on T10) while running. Rung R2 resets M190 via fault reset PB X1 and Rung R3 checks M190, but the rungs driving T10 and latching M190 are completely missing.
findings.proposed_fix: Add jam detection rungs before R2: energize T10 when entry eye X11 is blocked while Y10 is running ('LD X11', 'AND Y10', 'OUT T10 K50'), and latch M190 on timer done ('LD T10', 'SET M190').
findings.title: Missing conveyor jam detection logic and timer T10

findings.consequence: Unexpected automatic restart of the conveyor motor upon thermal recovery of the overload relay poses a severe pinch and crush hazard to maintenance personnel inspecting the stalled conveyor.
findings.evidence: In R1, M191 is driven with a standard 'OUT' coil directly from 'LDI X13'. In R2, fault reset PB X1 only resets M190. When motor overload MOL-1001 trips (X13 opens), M191 turns ON and stops Y10 via M199. If the thermal overload resets in the field, X13 recloses, de-energizing M191 and clearing M199 immediately. Because R4 maintains Y10 whenever Auto selector X2 is ON and M199 is clear, the conveyor restarts without operator intervention.
findings.proposed_fix: Latch the motor overload trip with 'SET M191' when X13 opens ('LDI X13', 'SET M191'). Require fault reset pushbutton X1 to reset M191 only after X13 has returned to healthy ('LD X1', 'AND X13', 'RST M191').
findings.title: Unlatched motor overload alarm allows unexpected automatic conveyor restart

findings.consequence: A release request from the line controller will drop the pallet stopper even when the cell is in E-stop, in manual maintenance mode, or faulted, potentially allowing pallets to roll unintentionally into the downstream station.
findings.evidence: Rung R6 sets stopper release solenoid Y11 directly on the rising edge of release request RQ-1005 ('LDP X14') without interlocking against E-stop healthy contact X0, Auto mode switch X2, or station fault summary M199.
findings.proposed_fix: Interlock Rung R6 with Auto mode, E-stop healthy, and no fault: 'LDP X14', 'AND X2', 'AND X0', 'ANI M199', 'SET Y11'.
findings.title: Stopper release solenoid Y11 lacks Auto mode and safety interlocks

findings.consequence: Maintenance personnel and controls engineers troubleshooting conveyor faults or motor trips cannot verify the meaning of M190 and M199 from the programming terminal, increasing diagnostic time and risk of erroneous edits.
findings.evidence: Internal relays M190 (reset in R2 and read in R3) and M199 (driven in R3 and interlocking Y10 in R4) have no symbol names or comments in device_comments. Key I/O devices X1, X13, and Y10 also lack entries in the station device comment table.
findings.proposed_fix: Add device comments for M190 ('ST10 conveyor jam alarm'), M199 ('ST10 summary fault / trip'), X1 ('Fault reset PB'), X13 ('Conveyor motor overload healthy'), and Y10 ('Conveyor motor contactor').
findings.title: Missing device comments for internal fault relays M190 and M199

data.summary: Engineering review of ST10 identified four defects: (1) jam detection logic (PE-1002/X11, timer T10 K50, and alarm latch M190) is completely missing despite parameter and cause-effect definitions; (2) motor overload alarm M191 is unlatched, allowing hazardous automatic restart upon thermal recovery without pressing fault reset PB X1; (3) stopper release solenoid Y11 actuates without Auto mode, E-stop, or fault interlocks; and (4) essential internal fault relays M190 and M199 lack device comments.
